title: Core Retail Transactions and Data Semantics
purpose: Every retail operation ultimately revolves around one thing: the transaction.
Inventory exists to support transactions. Promotions exist to influence transactions. Payments exist to complete transactions. Financial systems exist to account for transactions.
A deep understanding of transaction processing is the foundation of retail domain expertise.
learningOutcomes: Explain the complete basket lifecycle from scan to receipt
Understand pricing, promotions, taxes, and tender processing
Distinguish returns, refunds, exchanges, voids, and cancellations
Understand SKU, UOM, hierarchy, catalog, and price-book concepts
Translate retail business rules into system behavior
Understand business impact when transaction processing fails

sections.heading: Overview
points: A retail transaction is a sequence of business events that transforms customer intent into revenue.
Most customers think checkout is simple: Scan, Pay, Leave.

Reality: Scan -> Product Lookup -> Price Calculation -> Promotion Evaluation -> Tax Calculation -> Tender Selection -> Payment Processing -> Receipt Generation -> Inventory Update -> Sales Reporting -> Financial Posting.
One transaction can generate dozens of system events.

sections.heading: Business Importance
points: Transactions drive revenue, gross margin, tax calculation, inventory consumption, customer loyalty, financial reporting, and store performance.
Incorrect transactions create revenue leakage, inventory inaccuracy, tax errors, customer complaints, and audit risks.

sections.heading: Transaction Example
points: Customer purchases: 1 x Coke = $3, 1 x Chips = $2
Behind the scenes: Catalog Service, Pricing Engine, Promotion Engine, Tax Engine, Payment Processor, Receipt Service, Inventory Service, Analytics Platform, ERP Integration must all work correctly.

sections.heading: Transaction Event Timeline
points: Many production incidents can be isolated to a specific stage of this timeline.

sections.heading: What is Product Lookup?
points: When a barcode is scanned, POS retrieves product information.
Retrieved fields: SKU, Description, UOM, Department, Category, Tax Group, Price Group, Status.

sections.heading: Common Catalog Issues
points: Missing SKU: barcode scanned, product not found. Impact: cannot complete sale, manual intervention needed.
Duplicate barcode: two products mapped to one barcode. Impact: incorrect product sold.
Inactive product: product exists but status is inactive. Impact: unexpected checkout rejection.

sections.heading: Why Pricing Matters
points: Even a 1% pricing error can affect millions of dollars annually for large retailers.

sections.heading: Pricing Flow
points: Scan Item -> Identify Store -> Locate Price Book -> Retrieve Active Price -> Apply Overrides -> Display Price

sections.heading: Example
points: Same SKU, different stores, different prices.

sections.heading: Why Promotions Matter
points: Promotions influence revenue, customer retention, basket size, foot traffic, and inventory clearance.
Many retailers generate 20-40% of sales through promotional campaigns.

sections.heading: Promotion Evaluation Flow
points: Check Active Dates -> Check Store Eligibility -> Check Customer Eligibility -> Check Item Eligibility -> Determine Priority -> Determine Stackability -> Apply Discount

sections.heading: Promotion Concepts
points: Exclusions: alcohol, tobacco, gift cards, lottery.

sections.heading: Promotion Failure Example
points: Potential causes: promotion misconfiguration, POS bug, date validation failure, catalog mapping problem.

sections.heading: Why Taxes are Complex
points: Tax differs by country, state, city, county, product type, and customer type.

sections.heading: Tax Flow
points: Determine Tax Jurisdiction -> Determine Tax Group -> Retrieve Tax Rules -> Calculate Tax -> Apply Exemptions

sections.heading: Tender Definition
points: Examples: cash, debit card, credit card, gift card, store credit, mobile wallet, EBT.

sections.heading: Payment Ecosystem
points: Customer -> POS -> Gateway -> Card Network -> Issuer Bank -> Response

sections.heading: Purpose
points: Used for returns, fraud investigation, customer service, audit verification, and tax reporting.

sections.heading: Receipt Failure Example
points: Questions: can receipt be reprinted, was transaction saved, can return still occur?

chapters.title: Returns, Refunds, Exchanges, Voids, and Cancellations

sections.heading: Definitions
points: Return: customer gives item back, inventory usually increases.
Exchange: item replaced by another; one inventory up and one down.
Void: removes item before completion while sale continues.

sections.heading: Why States Matter
points: States determine allowed actions, recovery logic, and audit rules.

sections.heading: Standard State Flow
points: Created -> Scanning -> Pricing -> Promotion -> Tax -> Tender -> Authorization -> Completed

sections.heading: Recovery Paths
points: Payment Timeout -> Retry Once -> Retry Again -> Different Tender -> Cancel Transaction

sections.heading: What is Master Data?
points: Master data defines retail entities: products, stores, vendors, customers, price books, departments, categories.

sections.heading: SKU
points: Stock Keeping Unit: unique product identifier.

sections.heading: Master Data Failure Example
points: Result: incorrect tax, compliance risk, customer complaints.

sections.heading: Failure Cases
points: Price mismatch: shelf $5.99, POS $7.99 -> complaints, overrides, revenue loss.
Missing promotion: expected BOGO, applied none -> dissatisfaction, abandoned purchase.
Duplicate payment -> chargebacks, support calls, trust reduction.
Inventory not updated after sale -> stock drift, forecasting errors.
Transaction upload failure -> reporting errors, settlement mismatch, reconciliation issues.
Offline store -> delayed uploads, missing promotions, reconciliation work.

sections.heading: Pricing Validation Agent
points: Detects shelf price not matching POS price before customer impact.

sections.heading: Promotion Validation Agent
points: Checks promotion rules, date validity, and eligibility logic before deployment.

sections.heading: Payment Monitoring Agent
points: Identifies approval rate drops, timeout spikes, and gateway failures in real time.

sections.heading: Transaction RCA Agent
points: Inputs: POS logs, payment logs, support tickets, store alerts.
Outputs: root cause, severity, affected stores, recommended recovery action.

sections.heading: Checklist
points: Explain basket lifecycle from scan to receipt
Explain pricing, promotion, tax, and payment interactions
Differentiate return vs refund vs exchange vs void vs cancellation
Explain SKU, UOM, hierarchy, catalog, and price book
Explain business impact of transaction issues
Describe how AI agents can assist transaction operations

sections.heading: Study Estimate
points: Detailed enough for roughly 2 weeks (12-16 hours) and a strong foundation before Module 3.
